description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Found by /ship-it when the epic PR merged; main CI is red right now because of it.

Concrete failure: acknowledgments recorded as Spec-Ack commit trailers are destroyed the moment the PR lands, and the trunk gate then fails on findings that were legitimately acknowledged during development. Observed end to end today. Two release commits on the epic branch (26e3100, c9d1efe) carried Spec-Ack: change/uncovered_file=info. The PR was squash-merged as 5d9cb40. main now contains exactly two commits and ZERO Spec-Ack trailers. mix spec.check on main reports warnings=31 result=fail, locally and in CI, on the same 31 change/uncovered_file findings that passed as info one commit earlier.

Why this is not an edge case: squash is the default merge strategy across this fleet and is mandated by the ship workflow. Any team that acknowledges a finding during development loses that acknowledgment at merge, and their trunk goes red immediately afterward with no code change and no warning. The tool offers no migration path from a trailer to a durable record.

Related and same family: ancora-11w (a shallow clone hides trailers, so the gate silently resolves a different verdict). Both stem from acknowledgments living in commit messages, which CI checkouts and merge strategies routinely discard. Worth deciding them together.

Directions (decision needed, none chosen): teach the gate to look at the merge commit body as well, since squash preserves trailers there if the merge subject/body is composed to keep them; or move acknowledgment into a durable in-repo record (config severities or a per-subject override) and reduce the trailer to a development convenience that must be promoted before merge; or have the gate warn when it resolves an acknowledgment from a commit that is about to be squashed. The middle option matches the existing design intent, since the config file is already the reviewable place to record a standing severity decision.

Immediate remediation for this repo, separate from the design fix: the 31 findings are the known change/uncovered_file misfire on vendored priv/ assets and .eex templates (consolidated review finding F10 — the check uses hardcoded prefixes priv/, lib/, skills/, mix.exs and never consults lib_paths). Either fix F10 so those files stop being flagged, or record the demotion in .spec/config.yml severities where review can see it. Fixing F10 is the better answer and removes the need for the acknowledgment at all.

Cannot land on the epic branch: the branch is merged and deleted; this needs its own change against main, and the design decision above is unmade.

Status note (2026-09-03): the 'main CI is red right now' framing is stale. The push run on 5d9cb40 failed because the workflow compared against the repository default branch, which was the beadwork board branch at the time (finding F30, tracked in ancora-xla.5). The default branch is main now and the 13:17 workflow_dispatch run on main is green. The design defect described above is unchanged. Blocked by ancora-p47, which is the immediate remediation named in the last paragraph and is already implemented on branch ancora-p47/uncovered-lib-paths.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): where does a durable acknowledgment live so it survives a squash merge? Options in the description: also read the merge commit body; promote to an in-repo record (config severities or a per-subject override) with the trailer reduced to a development convenience; or warn when an acknowledgment comes from a commit about to be squashed.
Recommended default from the ticket: the middle option: .spec/config.yml severities and per-subject overrides are the durable, reviewable record; the trailer stays a development convenience and spec.check warns (named finding or stderr diagnostic) when a resolved acknowledgment exists only in a non-tip commit trailer. Decide together with ancora-11w.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.gate for acknowledgment resolution in test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/ancora/config_test.exs; a subprocess test in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs that squash-merges a branch carrying a trailer onto a trunk fixture and gates the trunk
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) an acknowledgment recorded the durable way (per ruling) produces the same severity on trunk after a squash merge as it did on the branch; (2) a trailer-only acknowledgment about to be lost is reported loudly, not silently dropped; (3) docs/migration.md and README describe the promotion step; (4) ancora.gate's acknowledgment requirements are edited substantively to state the rule
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.

Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

comments.text: RULING (Manuel, 2026-09-03): Option A. The durable acknowledgment record is the tree: .spec/config.yml severities and per-subject overrides. The Spec-Ack trailer stays a development convenience only. spec.check must warn loudly (a named finding or a stderr diagnostic, worker's call, but it must be impossible to miss) when a resolved acknowledgment exists only in a non-tip commit trailer, so a squash cannot drop it silently. Do not read the merge commit body. Document the promotion step in docs/migration.md and README. Edit ancora.gate's acknowledgment requirements substantively to state the rule. Pairs with the ancora-11w ruling (hard env failure on a shallow range).

Scheduling note from the ancora-gg8 architecture decision (2026-09-03): scope unchanged per the existing ruling (tree is the record, non-tip-trailer warning, documented promotion step, no merge-commit reading). Two additions from planning: implement in the same wave as ancora-gg8.5 (drift split + ack visibility) since they share the trailer/output vocabulary, and the promotion-step docs should name the requirement-scoped override key landing in ancora-gg8.1 as the narrowest durable target for a promoted ack.

test/ancora/trailer_test.exs:154 "an override repeated at the tip is not non-tip-only" pins the defining word "non-tip only". It commits Spec-Ack: derived/drift=warning on an earlier commit and Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info on the tip, then asserts result.overrides["derived/drift"] == :warning and result.non_tip_overrides == %{}. The empty map is the load-bearing half: it kills the mutation where parse_commits computes non_tip_overrides as "every override seen in any commit below HEAD" without Map.drop of the tip's keys, which would report drift as about to be lost when the tip repeats it. The companion edit at trailer_test.exs:124 asserts the positive shape %{"derived/drift" => :warning} on the pre-existing earlier-commit fixture, so both directions of the drop are pinned. Note that the reported severity comes from the union map, not from the non-tip commit that carried it, so oldest-wins precedence leaks into the warning text; that is pre-existing behavior and no test contradicts it.

test/ancora/gate_test.exs:459 "an applied trailer below the tip warns before squash" pins "loudly". It builds a real git fixture, puts Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info on the middle commit, adds a trailerless tip, runs Gate.check with base HEAD~2 inside capture_io(:stderr, ...), and asserts four separate substrings: "Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info", "non-tip commit", "lost by a squash merge", and ".spec/config.yml". This is not a non-empty-stderr check. It names the acknowledgment by code and severity and names the promotion target, so it kills a mutation that emits a generic diagnostic without identifying which ack is at risk, and one that drops the promotion target. It also asserts report.fail == false, pinning that the warning does not turn into a failing finding. The return value is routed through send(self(), ...) and assert_received so the Gate.check call stays inside the capture window; that is correct because Gate.check is synchronous, so assert_received without a timeout is the right choice.

test/ancora/gate_test.exs:486 "a non-tip trailer that resolves no finding does not warn" pins "resolved". The trailer is Spec-Ack: derived/growth=info on a non-tip commit while the diff produces derived/drift, so the override is genuinely present in the range and genuinely non-tip, and it is a valid registry code (trailer_test.exs:17 already proves derived/growth parses). It is not a trailer absent from the diff. report.fail == true confirms drift was not downgraded, and refute stderr =~ "lost by a squash merge" kills the mutation that warns for every key in non_tip_overrides regardless of whether it changed a finding's severity. Paired with gate_test.exs:431, whose tip-only trailer resolves drift from the trailer and asserts refute stderr =~ "lost by a squash merge", the two together kill the mutation that drops the non-tip condition and warns on every trailer-resolved finding.

test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:278 "promoted acknowledgment survives a squash merge" pins "survives a squash". The squash is real, not simulated: git checkout -b feature, a commit carrying Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info, then git checkout main, git merge --squash feature, and a commit made with -m so the SQUASH_MSG default that would have preserved the trailer is overridden. The trunk range therefore contains one trailerless commit, which is exactly what a GitHub squash merge produces. Both gates run through run_mix_subprocess, so the real mix spec.check task executes in a separate OS process. The proof is the severity_source pair: on the branch the drift finding is severity "info" with severity_source "trailer" and stderr carries the loss warning; on trunk the same finding is still "info" but severity_source is "config" and stderr no longer carries the warning. That asymmetry kills two mutations at once, the one where the gate reads the squash or merge commit body to recover the trailer (forbidden by the ruling, and it would leave severity_source at "trailer" on trunk), and the one where config severities are ignored once a trailer has ever applied. No test anywhere in the diff reads a merge commit body, and production still shells only git log base..HEAD --format=%B%x00, with no --first-parent and no SQUASH_MSG read.

Fixture hygiene and isolation are clean. Every fixture is built through test/support helpers (init_git_repo, write_files, write_config, write_decision, commit_all) or the System.cmd wrapper git!, and inspection goes through the systems under test, Gate.check and Trailer.read, never through a production helper pressed into fixture duty. Each test gets its own tmp root from the Ancora.TestCase setup. gate_test.exs and trailer_test.exs are async: false, which is required because capture_io on the named :stderr device is a global swap. spec_check_test.exs is async: true but each subprocess writes to its own uniquely named ANCORA_STDERR_FILE, so there is no shared stream. No tautologies: the squash test anchors branch_drift["severity"] == "info" independently before comparing trunk to it.

UNVERIFIED BY READING, three items. First, subprocess stderr delivery at spec_check_test.exs:305 and :317. Reading the wrapper shows exec mix "$@" 2>"$ANCORA_STDERR_FILE", so the redirect is declared, but that the gate's IO.puts(:stderr, ...) actually lands in that file is runtime behavior. The mutation to confirm it kills is changing IO.puts(:stderr, ...) at lib/ancora/gate.ex:507 to IO.puts(...); if stderr capture is not wired, that assertion passes anyway because the branch stderr check would have been vacuous. Second, IO capture interception in the two gate tests. Reading establishes the send/assert_received idiom keeps the call inside the capture window, but that ExUnit's named-device capture intercepts the write is runtime. Third, the premise of gate_test.exs:486, that derived/growth produces no finding for that fixture. The test is self-protecting here, since a growth finding would be downgraded by the trailer and would trip the refute, so a wrong premise fails rather than false-passes; still, only execution confirms it.

One non-blocking coverage gap for the auditor. The new production filter at lib/ancora/gate.ex:497 is a conjunction, finding.severity_source == :trailer and Map.has_key?(non_tip_overrides, finding.code), and the spec statement added at .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md requires both halves ("When a finding resolves through a trailer that exists only in a non-tip commit"). The second conjunct is isolated by gate_test.exs:431, where a trailer-resolved finding has an empty non_tip map. The first conjunct is not isolated: dropping severity_source == :trailer and keeping only the Map.has_key? test survives all four tests, because in gate_test.exs:486 no finding carries the code derived/growth at all, so the compound is false for the wrong reason. The scenario that would separate them is a non-tip trailer whose code matches a finding that config already pins at the same or a lower severity, so the trailer never applied and losing it costs nothing. Also unpinned: the Enum.uniq dedup, so nothing asserts the warning appears once when several findings share a code, and nothing asserts the [CONFIG] prefix that the rest of the trailer diagnostics carry. Separately, the squash test locks in that the warning still fires on the branch even though config already holds the same severity, which is a benign over-warn but is now a required behavior that a later noise-reduction change would have to break.

Gaps:
- Ruling condition not met, and the documented remedy does not work. Manuel's ruling and the orchestrator brief both require the loud warning to fire when an acknowledgment exists ONLY in a non-tip trailer, and not to fire once it has been promoted into .spec/config.yml. It fires in both cases. Built fixture f3: Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info on HEAD~1, severities: {derived/drift: info} committed at the tip. The real CLI still prints "Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info resolved from a non-tip commit and will be lost by a squash merge; promote it to .spec/config.yml before merging". Fixture f4 then squash-merges that exact tree onto trunk: derived/drift stays info, severity_source flips to config, stderr is clean, result=pass. So the warning states something false ("will be lost") and instructs a step the developer has already taken, with no documented way to clear it short of rewriting the trailer commit or repeating the trailer on the tip. README.md and docs/migration.md both tell the reader to promote and commit the config change, so following the shipped instructions leaves the alarm ringing forever. Mechanism: Ancora.Severity.resolve_tunable/3 at lib/ancora/severity.ex:159 keeps severity_source == :trailer whenever the trailer value is a legal non-raise, even when config independently supplies the same severity, and the new filter at lib/ancora/gate.ex:499 keys on exactly that. This is the deliverable contradicting itself: the same tree is reported as about to lose an acknowledgment and then demonstrably does not lose it.
- The test suite pins the false positive. test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:326 asserts branch.stderr =~ "lost by a squash merge" on the branch AFTER write_config promoted the severity, and :339 asserts the trunk run is clean. Those two assertions describe the same tree. A fix for Gap 1 would have to delete assertion :326, so the suite cannot catch the defect today.
- Corpus rule violation on the new ADR filename. .spec/decisions/README.md states "One file per ADR, named `<id>.md`" and all ten siblings comply (ancora.decision.*.md). The new file is .spec/decisions/durable-acknowledgments.md while its id is ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments. mix spec.validate passes and the affects: entries resolve, because ADRs load through a Path.wildcard at lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex:68 and lib/ancora/status.ex:46 that ignores the filename, so this is a rule the tool does not enforce. It is still a stated rule of the corpus this ticket edits. Rename to ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments.md.

Notes:
- The parts that work, verified by execution, not by reading. Fixture f1 (trailer on HEAD~1, bare tip) warns and passes. Fixture f2 (same override repeated on the tip) is silent. Fixture f4 proves the whole point of the ticket: a promoted acknowledgment survives a squash merge with severity_source == config and a clean verdict. The trailer union precedence is unchanged by the rewrite from a single parse of the concatenated log to a per-commit parse plus Map.merge, since both resolve ties to the oldest commit in the range.
- On "nothing reads the merge commit body": this ticket adds no merge-body path, and the ADR's sentence about no separate recovery path is accurate. Worth recording that the pre-existing generic range read does pick up a merge commit body, since git log base..HEAD includes merge commits. Fixture f6 puts Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info in a --no-ff merge commit message and the gate applies it with severity_source trailer. That behavior predates 849dbf9 and is out of scope here.
- Ancora.Trailer.parse_commits/1 splits git log --format=%B%x00 on NUL with trim: true, then treats List.first as the tip. A commit created with --allow-empty-message would produce an empty first segment that trim discards, shifting "tip" onto the second commit and suppressing a warning that should fire. Rare enough that it does not move the verdict.
- No direct test covers an invalid trailer code appearing below the tip. The implementation is correct by construction, since invalid codes never enter overrides and non_tip_overrides is derived from overrides.
